To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the peptide F0T8 is a good model for studying the formation of a helix– turn–helix structure.

the formation of a helix-turn-helix structure is a very fast event (on the order of a few tens of nanoseconds) and that the dynamics of this process are strongly affected by the solvent viscosity and by the presence of an organized medium.

the formation of a helix– turn–helix structure in a membrane-active peptide, trichogine, is a fast process that takes place on the microsecond time scale, and that the formation of the turn region is a rate-limiting step.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the investigation of a new analogue of Trichogin, a membrane-active peptide, with the sequence F0T8: F0T8 has been synthesized by solid phase peptide synthesis (SPPS) using Fmoc chemistry, with a final cleavage from the solid support by hydrogen fluoride.
the study of the dynamics of the folding of a helix– turn–helix structure.

the study of the dynamics of formation of a helix– turn–helix (H3) structure in a membrane-active peptide, by means of time-resolved optical techniques, from the sub-nanosecond to the sub-microsecond timescale.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CD spectra of F0 and F0T8 are quite similar in all the solvents investigated.
the peptide investigated in the different environments is basically in equilibrium among the following states: 310-helix (in methanol), 310-a-helix (in Glc/MeOH and SDS), and random coil (in Glc).
, in all three solvents, the peptide shows a mixed 310/a helical structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the F0T8 peptide in SDS micelles, in methanol, and even in the viscous solvent Glc/methanol (8: 2), exhibits a high content of 310-helix and a low content of a-helix, as revealed by CD spectroscopy, in good agreement with the X-ray diffraction data for the solid phase of trichogins GA IV.
the peptide is in a helix–helix equilibrium in all solvents investigated.
the F0T8 structure is not a simple 310-helix but rather a helix–loop–helix structure, with a hinge point between Gly5 and Gly6.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of a helix– turn–helix structure in F0T8 is a slow process, with a time scale of the order of microseconds.
F0T8 exhibits a complex behaviour in terms of conformational dynamics, which depends on the solvent and the temperature.
the conformational equilibrium of F0T was found to be strongly solvent-dependent.
